facts.text: Fultondale began in the early 1900s as Fulton Springs, a modest mining community that grew around coal extraction.
In the 1870s, entrepreneur Bartholomew Boyle bought 2,000 acres and opened coal mines named after his daughter Mary Lee.
Fultondale was created when the towns of Lewisburg, Glendale, and Fulton Springs merged into one municipality.
The city officially incorporated in 1947, solidifying its status as a distinct community within Jefferson County.
Before Interstate 65, US 31 was the main northbound route from Birmingham to Nashville, and its old alignment—now Stouts Road—still traces through Fultondale.
On the city’s southern edge once stood the Skyview drive‑in theatre, one of only a few in the Birmingham area, before it was demolished when I‑65 was built.
